From f75c9f110f0bc2cba401a8b95c9c4377c6c057e9 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eran Mizrahi <eranmizra@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Apr 2011 21:10:37 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] RTL: Fix handling of special unicode marker 0xFEFF

This fixes a problem introduced by commit 43e45eb94e1
which (wrongly) handled the 0xFEFF mark as RTL.

Change-Id: Icf8fce91e6df8c4fa8e01eb893174a9fdb8c0766

diff --git a/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java b/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
index 88f72594567..54bb57f0a80 100644
--- a/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
+++ b/core/java/android/text/TextUtils.java
@@ -1692,7 +1692,7 @@ public class TextUtils {
                (c >= 0xFB1D && c <= 0xFB4F) ||
                (c >= 0x0600 && c <= 0x07BF) ||
                (c >= 0xFB50 && c <= 0xFDFF) ||
-               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)    ;
+               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFE)    ;
     }
 
     /**
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `TextUtils.java`**
- A single line of code was modified in the `isRtlCharacter` method. The condition that checks for the range of characters now excludes the special Unicode marker `0xFEFF`. 
- The original line:
  ```java
  (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)
  ```
  was changed to:
  ```java
  (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFE)
  ```

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The modification in `TextUtils.java` addresses a bug introduced by a previous commit (43e45eb94e1) that incorrectly treated the Unicode marker `0xFEFF` as a right-to-left (RTL) character. By adjusting the character range to exclude `0xFEFF`, the patch corrects the handling of this special marker, ensuring that it is not misclassified in the context of text directionality. This change is crucial for proper text rendering and processing in applications that utilize this utility.

RTL: Fix handling of special unicode marker 0xFEFF

Change-Id: Icf8fce91e6df8c4fa8e01eb893174a9fdb8c0766

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect handling of the Unicode marker `0xFEFF`, which was mistakenly classified as a right-to-left (RTL) character due to an inclusive range check in the `isRtlCharacter` method. This led to improper text directionality handling in applications that rely on this utility for text processing.

Here is the patch:
 
     public static boolean isRTLCharacter(char c) {
         //range of RTL characters per unicode specification
         return (c >= 0x0590 && c <= 0x05FF) ||
                (c >= 0xFB1D && c <= 0xFB4F) ||
                (c >= 0x0600 && c <= 0x07BF) ||
                (c >= 0xFB50 && c <= 0xFDFF) ||
-               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFF)    ;
+               (c >= 0xFE70 && c <= 0xFEFE)    ;
     }
